One gap: the attachment records in this dataset carry no explicit url/link field, so c3 can't be mechanically checked against the data the way c1 and c2 can — it has to be inferred from context (issue description, id naming). This matters here because WEB-14 has two attachments with the identical title 'Deploy runbook' (att-web14-runbook and att-web14-prod); the author's conditions correctly identify the URL as the disambiguator, but the records as given don't let a tool query that field directly, so a careful agent would need to fetch/verify the actual link before renaming rather than assuming the first title match.

ambiguity_effects.explain: In a Linear context 'rename the attachment' unambiguously means updating the attachment's title field on the issue, not editing content at the external URL. Both readings point to the same action on the same record, so this doesn't affect which record is targeted.

Exact-title matching is the natural reading and both plausible candidates (att-web14-runbook, att-web14-prod) match exactly anyway, so a loose-vs-exact reading doesn't change which records are in play; the real disambiguator is the URL (c3), not title strictness.
